data.name: Perseus
data.gender_notes: Perseus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Perseus is a hero known for saving Andromeda from a sea monster. In Christian tradition, Perseus represents salvation, bravery, and divinely given abilities to overcome challenges. The name Perseus carries the meaning “Hero, Savior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Perseus usually hope their child will grow to embody hero, savior and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Perseus total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: פרסאוס
in_hebrew.meaning: הוא שמו של גיבור במיתולוגיה היוונית
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פרסאוס הוא שם של גיבור במיתולוגיה היוונית, בנו של זאוס, המלך של האלים. הוא היה ידוע בניצחונו על מדוזה והצלתה של אנדרומדה. השם פרסאוס נגזר מהמילה היוונית פרסאוס, שפירושה 'הואשם' או 'מחוספס'. למרות היותו דמות מיתולוגית, פרסאוס הפך לדמות חשובה בתרבות היוונית והרומית, והוא מוזכר גם בכתבי היסטוריונים ומשוררים עתיקים.

in_greek.name: Περσεύς
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Περσεύς ήταν μεγάλος ήρωας στην ελληνική μυθολογία, γιος του Δία και της Δαναής. Είναι γνωστός για την τομή το κεφαλής της Μέδουσας και τη σωτηρία της Ανδρομέδας. Το όνομα Περσεύς προέρχεται από το ελληνικό ρήμα 'περσεύω', που σημαίνει 'να καταστρέφω' ή 'να κόβω'. Ο Περσεύς ήταν σημαντική προσωπικότητα στην αρχαία ελληνική κουλτούρα και αναφέρεται σε πολλά έργα της αρχαίας ελληνικής λογοτεχνίας.

in_latin.name: Perseus
in_latin.long_meaning: Perseus, a hero from Greek mythology, was the son of Zeus and Danaë. He was renowned for beheading Medusa and saving Andromeda. The name Perseus is derived from the Greek verb 'perseuō', meaning 'to destroy' or 'to cut off'. As a significant figure in ancient Greek culture, Perseus was mentioned in numerous works of ancient literature and history, and his legend was later adopted into Roman mythology.

in_english.name: Perseus
in_english.meaning: A hero from Greek mythology, destroyer of evil
in_english.long_meaning: Perseus is a name with roots in Greek mythology, derived from the verb 'perseuō', meaning 'to destroy' or 'to cut off'. In mythology, Perseus was the son of Zeus and a hero known for beheading Medusa and saving Andromeda. The name Perseus symbolizes bravery, heroism, and the triumph of good over evil. While not directly mentioned in the Bible, the story of Perseus has been influential in Western culture and continues to inspire artistic and literary works.

data.cultural_impact: Perseus is a renowned hero in Greek mythology, revered for his courage, resourcefulness, and bravery. He is the son of Zeus and Danae, born in extraordinary circumstances involving a nuclear-level miracle and an escape from an enraged king. Later, Perseus would go on to save the beautiful princess Andromeda from the deadly sea monster Cetus, and secure her hand in marriage. This legend has been depicted in countless paintings, sculptures, and stories, inspiring human generations to emulate the heroic deeds of Perseus.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, Perseus can be seen as a symbol of salvation and overcoming challenges with the help of divine intervention. The story of Perseus resonates with the Bible narrative of facing trials and conquering them with faith and trust in God. Just as Perseus navigated through his trials in securing the hand of Andromeda, Christians too face their own obstacles and are called to trust that God will lead them to victory. In this sense, Perseus represents the idea that through divine intervention, we can all be heroes in our own lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Perseus is the mythological hero who beheaded Medusa, the Gorgon, and saved Andromeda from a sea monster. His name symbolizes courage and victory over fearsome monsters, embodying the Christian ideals of strength in the face of adversity and triumph against evil.

biblical_reference.note: The name Perseus is not mentioned in the Bible.

historical_references.reference: Perseus is a hero of ancient Greek mythology, the son of Zeus and Danae. He is best known for saving his mother and his grandmother Danaë from the wrath of King Acrisius of Argos, who had been told by an oracle that he would be killed by a son born to Danaë. Perseus was sent away in a chest, which was cast out to sea. He was eventually found by the fisherman Dictys, who brought him up on the island of Seriphus.

According to legend, Perseus then went on to slay the Gorgon Medusa and save Andromeda from being sacrificed to a sea monster. These adventures are recounted in Apollodorus' Library, a major source for Greek mythology.
